notes: PSA 5.8 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.11. Prostate volume 54 mL. csPCa 0.48.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following rising PSA and persistent severe lower urinary tract symptoms.

Recently retired farmer with a history of hypercholesterolaemia and coronary artery disease, currently managed on atorvastatin and rosuvastatin. He lives with his partner and remains active with light weight-training twice weekly. He reports severe lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 23/35, significantly impacting his quality of life. He has a history of anxiety regarding medical procedures and requests additional time for consultations. Recent dental check-ups and a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins have been completed. He denies any bone pain, haematuria, or neurological symptoms. He continues to smoke occasionally but quit regular smoking in 2015 after a 10 pack-year history.

On digital rectal examination, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged, smooth, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with normal cardiovascular and respiratory findings. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no palpable masses or organomegaly.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
